title: Benchmark for Refusal Calibration: When Models Over-Refuse

novelty_assessment.label: already_solved
novelty_assessment.reasoning: OR-Bench (ICML 2025) provides exactly this: 80,000 seemingly toxic but benign prompts across 10 rejection categories, with a 1,000-prompt hard subset and 600 toxic control prompts. The paper measures refusal rates across models and establishes the safety-over-refusal tradeoff (Spearman correlation 0.89). FalseReject benchmarks 29 state-of-the-art LLMs on over-refusal. SafeConstellations (arXiv:2508.11290, 2025) and ACTOR provide mitigation frameworks. The proposed 200-prompt benchmark is a strict subset of OR-Bench's 80,000-prompt study, both in scale and methodology.

title: Benchmark Saturation Analysis: Tracking Ceiling Effects Across Safety Benchmarks

novelty_assessment.label: mostly_novel
novelty_assessment.reasoning: While benchmark saturation is a well-known phenomenon for capability benchmarks (MMLU, GSM8K), a systematic saturation analysis specifically for safety benchmarks (HELM Safety, AILuminate) has not been published. The AILuminate grading system (Poor to Excellent) and HELM Safety leaderboard provide the raw data, but no published work computes score distributions, variance over time, pairwise model distinguishability, or identifies which specific hazard categories are approaching ceiling effects in safety evaluations. The concept is well-established from capability benchmarks, but the application to safety benchmarks is a timely and unfilled gap.

title: Data Contamination Investigation in Safety Benchmarks

novelty_assessment.label: mostly_novel
novelty_assessment.reasoning: Data contamination detection methods (min-k%, n-gram overlap, perplexity) are well-established and have been applied extensively to capability benchmarks. However, a systematic contamination analysis of safety benchmarks specifically (AILuminate, HELM Safety) has not been published. AntiLeak-Bench (ACL 2025) provides contamination-free evaluation methodology but does not analyze existing safety benchmarks for contamination. The ICML 2025 paper 'How Much Can We Forget about Data Contamination?' shows contamination effects can be moderate, but this has not been tested in the safety domain. The specific application of contamination detection to safety evaluation scores is a novel and impactful contribution.
